method_card.title: Social Media and Online Life
method_card.content:
This lesson covers social media vocabulary, daily online activities, and the advantages and disadvantages of digital life. It also drills relative pronouns and balanced argument structures.

GermanEnglish
das Handy / das Smartphonemobile phone / smartphone
die sozialen Medien (pl.)social media
teilento share
postento post
folgen (+ dative)to follow
der Follower / die Followerinfollower
Fotos hochladen (separable)to upload photos
Nachrichten schickento send messages
im Internet surfento surf the internet
in Kontakt bleibento stay in contact
das Cybermobbingcyberbullying (Higher)
die Bildschirmzeitscreen time (Higher)
der Datenschutzdata protection (Higher)
nützlichuseful
süchtig machendaddictive
einerseits ... andererseitson one hand ... on the other hand

Grammar focus — Relative pronouns (der/die/das + verb at end): German relative pronouns agree in gender with the noun they refer back to, but their case depends on their role in the relative clause. Nominative subject: die App, die ich am meisten benutze (die App is feminine → relative pronoun is die). Note: after the relative pronoun, the verb goes to the end of the relative clause — just like weil and dass. Common forms: masculine nom. der, fem. nom. die, neut. nom. das; masc. acc. den, fem. acc. die, neut. acc. das.

Grammar focus — hochladen (separable): hochladen = to upload. In a main clause the prefix splits: Ich lade Fotos hoch. (I upload photos.) In a subordinate clause it stays whole: weil ich Fotos hochlade.

Model paragraph: Einerseits sind soziale Medien nützlich, weil man mit Freunden in Kontakt bleiben kann. Andererseits verbringt man zu viel Zeit am Handy und das Cybermobbing, das ein großes Problem ist, macht mir Sorgen. (On one hand, social media is useful because you can stay in contact with friends. On the other hand, you spend too much time on your phone and cyberbullying, which is a big problem, worries me.)
steps: Learn the social media vocabulary including noun genders (der/die/das)
Master hochladen as a separable verb: Ich lade Fotos hoch (main clause) vs weil ich Fotos hochlade (subordinate)
Practise relative pronouns: use der/die/das to match the noun's gender, then send the verb to the end
Build balanced arguments using einerseits ... andererseits with weil clauses
Use Man sollte / Man kann + infinitive at the end for impersonal advice structures

exam_context.frequency: Very common — especially in extended writing and Higher speaking tasks

worked_examples.question: Translate into English: 'Ich verbringe jeden Tag ungefähr zwei Stunden am Handy.'

steps.label: Key vocabulary
steps.content: verbringe (from verbringen) = spend (time). jeden Tag = every day. ungefähr = approximately. am Handy = on my phone (an + dem Handy — dative after an for static location).

steps.label: False friend alert
steps.content: das Handy = mobile phone (NOT 'handy'). Don't confuse with das Telefon which usually means a landline.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I spend about two hours a day on my phone.

worked_examples.question: How do you write a balanced argument about social media in German using einerseits/andererseits?

steps.label: Advantage with weil
steps.content: Einerseits sind soziale Medien nützlich, weil man mit Freunden in Kontakt bleiben kann. (weil + verb at end: kann)

steps.label: Disadvantage
steps.content: Andererseits verbringt man zu viel Zeit am Bildschirm und das kann ungesund sein. (man = impersonal 'you/one')

steps.label: Personal opinion
steps.content: Ich bin der Meinung, dass man vorsichtig sein muss. (dass + verb at end: muss)

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Einerseits sind soziale Medien nützlich, weil man mit Freunden in Kontakt bleiben kann. Andererseits verbringt man zu viel Zeit am Bildschirm und das kann ungesund sein. Ich bin der Meinung, dass man vorsichtig sein muss.

bronze.question: Match the German to the English meaning
Match the German to the English meaning
Complete the sentence with the correct word

gaps.correct_explain: Handy (or Smartphone) = mobile phone. Handy is a false friend — it does NOT mean 'handy' in English.

wrong.Telefon: Telefon usually means a landline telephone, not a mobile. The German word for mobile phone is Handy.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence with the correct word
sentence_parts: ist ein großes Problem für junge Leute.

gaps.correct_explain: Cybermobbing = cyberbullying. It is a key vocabulary item for the social media topic.

wrong.Datenschutz: Datenschutz means 'data protection'. While important, the term for online bullying is Cybermobbing.

bronze.question: What does 'Man kann mit Freunden in Kontakt bleiben' mean?
options: You can stay in contact with friends
You can make new friends online
You must stay in contact with your friends
You cannot stay in contact with friends

bronze.question: What does 'Soziale Medien können süchtig machen' mean?
options: Social media is fun for everyone
Social media is dangerous for children

bronze.source_text: Ich schaue gern Videos online und schicke meinen Freunden Nachrichten.
model_answers: I like watching videos online and send messages to my friends.
hints: meinen Freunden = to my friends (dative plural)

bronze.question: Listen and type what you hear
bronze.audio_text: Ich benutze mein Handy jeden Tag.
bronze.correct_text: Ich benutze mein Handy jeden Tag.
bronze.translation: I use my phone every day.

silver.question: Complete the sentence — type the missing words
silver.english: I **spend** too much time on my phone and my parents think I **should** go outside more.
sentence_parts: zu viel Zeit am Handy und meine Eltern finden, dass ich mehr nach draußen gehen

gaps.rule: Verb conjugation — ich form of verbringen
gaps.correct_explain: verbringe is the ich form of verbringen (to spend time).

gaps.rule: Modal verb — should (Konjunktiv II) in dass clause
gaps.correct_explain: sollte = should (Konjunktiv II of sollen). After dass, the conjugated verb goes to the end of the clause.

wrong.soll: soll is present tense ('is supposed to'). For 'should' (advice), use sollte.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Ich bin der Meinung, dass soziale Medien sind nützlich.
silver.error_type: Word order — verb-final in dass clause
silver.explanation: After dass, the conjugated verb must go to the end of the clause. Correct: dass soziale Medien nützlich sind — NOT dass soziale Medien sind nützlich.
silver.translation: I am of the opinion that social media is useful.

distractor_labels.kann: wrong verb form — Medien is plural, so the modal verb needs the plural form können, not kann (singular)

silver.source_text: I upload photos on Instagram and send messages to my friends.
model_answers: Ich lade Fotos auf Instagram hoch und schicke meinen Freunden Nachrichten.
hints: to my friends = meinen Freunden (dative plural)

silver.question: Listen and type what you hear
silver.audio_text: Cybermobbing ist ein großes Problem für junge Leute.
silver.correct_text: Cybermobbing ist ein großes Problem für junge Leute.
silver.translation: Cyberbullying is a big problem for young people.

silver.question: Put these words in the correct order to form a sentence

gold.source_text: On the one hand, social media is useful because you can stay in contact with friends. On the other hand, you spend too much time on your phone and cyberbullying is a serious problem that can be very harmful.
model_answers: Einerseits sind soziale Medien nützlich, weil man mit Freunden in Kontakt bleiben kann. Andererseits verbringt man zu viel Zeit am Handy und Cybermobbing ist ein ernstes Problem, das sehr schädlich sein kann.

gold.question: Build the sentence in German
gold.english: Although I like using social media, I think one should be careful.

distractor_labels.den: wrong — soziale Medien takes no article; den would be a masculine accusative article which is not needed here
distractor_labels.soll: wrong mood — sollte (should, Konjunktiv II) is more appropriate for advice than soll (present tense 'is supposed to')
distractor_labels.benutzt: wrong verb form — after obwohl the subject is ich, so benutze (not benutzt, which is du/er/sie/es)

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are at a tourist information office in a German town. You want to find out about safe internet use for young people and local digital workshops.

bullets.prompt: Greet the member of staff and ask if there are any workshops about internet safety for young people.
bullets.model_answer: Guten Tag! Gibt es Workshops zum Thema Internetsicherheit für junge Leute?
bullets.note: Guten Tag (formal greeting) + Gibt es...? (Are there...?) + zum Thema (on the topic of) + für + accusative

bullets.prompt: Say you use social media every day and you think it can be addictive.
bullets.model_answer: Ich benutze soziale Medien jeden Tag und ich finde, dass sie süchtig machen können.
bullets.note: dass + verb-final: machen können (modal at end, infinitive before it in a dass clause with modal)

bullets.prompt: Give one advantage of social media.
bullets.model_answer: Einerseits sind soziale Medien nützlich, weil man mit Freunden in Kontakt bleiben kann.
bullets.note: einerseits + weil + verb-final (kann at end); man (impersonal subject)

bullets.prompt: Say what you will do to protect your data online in future.
bullets.model_answer: In Zukunft werde ich weniger persönliche Informationen im Internet teilen.
bullets.note: werden + infinitive for future (teilen at end); weniger (less) + personal information; in Zukunft = in future

gold.question: Listen and type what you hear
gold.audio_text: Obwohl ich gern soziale Medien benutze, bin ich der Meinung, dass man vorsichtig sein muss.
gold.correct_text: Obwohl ich gern soziale Medien benutze, bin ich der Meinung, dass man vorsichtig sein muss.
gold.translation: Although I like using social media, I am of the opinion that one must be careful.

gold.question: Complete the sentence — type the missing words (Higher: modal verbs + impersonal man)
gold.english: One **should** never share personal information and one **must** be careful online.
sentence_parts: nie persönliche Informationen teilen und man

gaps.correct_explain: sollte = should (Konjunktiv II of sollen). With man (impersonal 'one'), it stays as sollte (third person singular). Used for advice.

wrong.muss: muss means 'must' — that is used in the second gap. 'Should' = sollte (Konjunktiv II).
wrong.soll: soll is present tense ('is supposed to'). For giving advice ('should'), use the conditional: sollte.

gaps.correct_explain: muss = must (obligation). Man muss vorsichtig sein = one must be careful.

wrong.kann: kann means 'can' (ability). The sentence requires 'must' for obligation: muss.
